subject: simple binomial model crashing on Windows cluster and not on personal machine

messages.author: f1572a038d61492c
messages.subject: simple binomial model crashing on Windows cluster and not on personal machine
parts:
Hi all,

I'm fitting here a logistic regression model with one binary covariate and one multilevel categorical variable and one independent random effect. The model fits fine on my machine (Mac Airbook 2015, 8 GB / 1.6 GHz). However, I'm fitting other models and some with larger data sets so I started to move my work over to a Windows-based cluster at work (per the website: Each cluster node is a Dell PowerEdge M640 or C6320 Blade server with 16 2.00GHz Intel Xeon CPUs and 384GB or more RAM.) It consistently crashes. When run with verbose = TRUE, it stops around here 

Gaussian approximation:
tolerance_func = 0.0005
tolerance_step = 0.0005
optpar_fp = 0
optpar_nr_step_factor = -0.1
Gaussian data: No

Anyone know what might be causing this? I attempted to attach the data file and script but kept getting an error. The script is below and perhaps I can email the data file if someone is interested.

library(INLA)

load('example.rda')

formula <- infant.death ~ as.factor(v024) +
  sex + 
  + f(v001, model = 'iid')

inlamod.inf.sex <- inla(formula, family = 'binomial',
                        data = model.data, verbose = TRUE, 
                        num.threads = 2)

summary(inlamod.inf.sex)

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] simple binomial model crashing on Windows cluster and not on personal machine
parts:
Hi there,

it seems like Windows does not run R-INLA well for larger models, and
its not clear why this happens or something can be done to fix this. We
have severely limited experience with Windows (never used it regularly
myself), so its all about if we can get some expert help... 

see also
https://www.r-inla.org/news#h.zfhs4mwsjweq
about 'windows builder', but there is no success so far.


what have been reported to work well, is to install Linux on your server
using Windows Subsystem for Linux and run R and R-INLA there, see f.ex

https://fedoramagazine.org/wsl-fedora-33/

or some other linux distro. This should work well right out of the box.

Or if you have access to another Linux server.

Please let us know how this goes

Best
H
